title: Cohomology of the sequential derived limit
statement:
Let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, let
$\cdots\to K_2\xrightarrow{t_1}K_1\xrightarrow{t_0}K_0$ be a tower of complexes of
$\mathcal R$-modules, $T\colon\prod_nK_n\to\prod_nK_n$, $T((k_n)_n)=(t_n(k_{n+1}))_n$, and
$R\varprojlim_nK_n:=\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1]$.

1. For every $q$ there is a natural short exact sequence of sheaves

   $$
   0\to\coker\Bigl(\prod_nH^{q-1}(K_n)\xrightarrow{1-T}\prod_nH^{q-1}(K_n)\Bigr)
   \to H^q\bigl(R\varprojlim_nK_n\bigr)\to\varprojlim_nH^q(K_n)\to0 .
   $$

2. For a tower of modules $(M_n)$ (complexes in degree $0$), $R^p\varprojlim_nM_n:=
   H^p(R\varprojlim_nM_n)$ is $\varprojlim_nM_n$ for $p=0$,
   $\coker(1-T)$ for $p=1$, and $0$ for $p\notin\{0,1\}$.
3. Consequently the sequence in 1 is the Milnor sequence
   $0\to R^1\varprojlim_nH^{q-1}(K_n)\to H^q(R\varprojlim_nK_n)\to\varprojlim_nH^q(K_n)\to0$.

proof.text:
Work in the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with the usual universe convention for the pro-etale site. For a map of complexes $\varphi:A\to B$, put $D=\operatorname{Cone}(\varphi)[-1]$. The cone triangle $A\xrightarrow{\varphi}B\to\operatorname{Cone}(\varphi)\to A[1]$ is distinguished by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], using $H^{q-1}(\operatorname{Cone}(\varphi))=H^q(D)$, contains
$$
H^{q-1}(A)\xrightarrow{H^{q-1}\varphi}H^{q-1}(B)\xrightarrow{\beta}H^q(D)\xrightarrow{\gamma}H^q(A)\xrightarrow{H^q\varphi}H^q(B).
$$
Exactness identifies $\operatorname{coker}(H^{q-1}\varphi)$ with $\operatorname{im}\beta=\ker\gamma$ and $\operatorname{im}\gamma$ with $\ker(H^q\varphi)$; hence it gives the required short exact sequence with these two end terms. All kernels, cokernels and images here are in the sheaf category, not cokernels of sections.

Apply this to $A=B=\prod_nK_n$ and $\varphi=1-T$. The product/cohomology identification is supplied by [det-pe-products-derived]. To verify explicitly that the canonical comparison induced by projections is an isomorphism, use exactness of products [det-pe-products-exact]. Put $Z_n^q=\ker d_n^q$ and $B_n^q=\operatorname{im}d_n^{q-1}$. Products preserve kernels; applying exactness to $0\to\ker d_n^{q-1}\to K_n^{q-1}\to B_n^q\to0$ shows that the boundaries of the product complex are $\prod_nB_n^q$. Applying it to $0\to B_n^q\to Z_n^q\to H^q(K_n)\to0$ identifies its cohomology with $\prod_nH^q(K_n)$ by the coordinate projections. Its $n$-th component is therefore $H^q(\pi_n)$, so
$$
H^q(\pi_n)H^q(1-T)=H^q(\pi_n)-H^q(t_n)H^q(\pi_{n+1}).
$$
Thus $H^q(1-T)$ identifies with $1-T$ on $\prod_nH^q(K_n)$. By [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], reindexed from $r\geq1$ to $n\geq0$, its kernel has sections $(h_n)$ satisfying $h_n=H^q(t_n)(h_{n+1})$, with componentwise restrictions, and is $\varprojlim_nH^q(K_n)$. This proves clause 1.

For naturality, a morphism of towers $(f_n):(K_n,t_n)\to(K'_n,t'_n)$ satisfies $f_nt_n=t'_nf_{n+1}$, so $F=\prod_nf_n$ satisfies $F(1-T)=(1-T')F$. Write $D^q=A^q\oplus B^{q-1}$, with differential $(a,b)\mapsto(d_Aa,-d_Bb-\varphi a)$, using the cone and shift formulas in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The induced cone map is $(a,b)\mapsto(Fa,Fb)$. For the cited cone triangle with last map $-p$, the maps adjacent to $H^q(D)$ are induced by the inclusion $b\mapsto(0,b)$ and the negative projection $(a,b)\mapsto-a$, respectively. The cone map commutes with both maps, since $(Fa,Fb)$ has second coordinate $Fb$ and negative first coordinate $-Fa=F(-a)$. Passing to cohomology and then factoring through the above cokernel and kernel therefore gives a commuting diagram of short exact sequences. The coordinate projections commute with $F$, so the product and inverse-limit identifications in that diagram are natural as well.

For clause 2, $P=\prod_nM_n$ is concentrated in degree $0$. By the cone and shift formulas of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1]$ has $P$ in degrees $0,1$, zero in every other degree, and differential $-(1-T):P\to P$. Multiplication by $-1$ in degree $1$ identifies it with the two-term complex having differential $1-T$. Therefore $H^0=\ker(1-T)$, $H^1=\operatorname{coker}(1-T)$ and $H^p=0$ for $p\notin\{0,1\}$. The sectionwise formula of [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] identifies this kernel with $\varprojlim_nM_n$. The notation $R^p\varprojlim$ in the statement is defined as this cohomology, so clause 2 follows without an additional assertion about derived functors. Finally apply clause 2 to $M_n=H^{q-1}(K_n)$ and its induced transition maps, and substitute its $R^1\varprojlim=\operatorname{coker}(1-T)$ into clause 1 to obtain clause 3.
